clue.text: Yank wearing waistcoat

parts.note: to yank is to pull sharply, to jerk
someone wearing a coat is in it

explanation.surface: An American is dressed in a waistcoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American, but it is the verb meaning to pull sharply.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerkin is a close-fitting sleeveless jacket, a kind of vest or waistcoat.

clue.text: Brilliant display of English toiletry set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is raised, read from bottom to top

parts.note: talc is a powder used as a toiletry

explanation.surface: A showy array of English bathroom products is laid out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' works as a reversal only because this is a down entry, so the powder is read upward; 'Brilliant' is part of the definition, not an adjective on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is dazzling success or a conspicuous show of brilliance, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Equipment, new, introduced to encourage army leader

parts.note: kit is a set of equipment

indicators.note: one letter is introduced into another word, put inside it

parts.note: to cheer is to encourage

explanation.surface: Fresh gear is brought in to hearten a commander's troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduced to' places the new letter inside, just after CHE. Lord Kitchener was the British field marshal on the famous First World War recruiting poster.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert Kitchener was a British field marshal and Secretary of State for War, a famous military commander.

clue.text: Description of creed — commendable, with and without content

parts.note: nice means pleasing, worthy of approval

indicators.note: content is what lies inside, so the middle letters of the word are removed, leaving only its ends

parts.note: the same word nice, used a second time

explanation.surface: A creed is called praiseworthy, both with and without substance.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is that 'with and without content' applies to the same word twice: first whole, then emptied by 'without content', which keeps only its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nicene Creed, agreed at the Council of Nicaea, is the Christian statement of faith, so Nicene describes that creed.

clue.text: Clamp down on drink given to journalists

parts.note: to sup is to drink, or a sip of drink
the press are journalists collectively

explanation.surface: A crackdown on alcohol handed out to reporters.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppress is to put down forcibly, to crush or stifle, the same as a crackdown.

clue.text: Standard dress — it's spartan when redesigned

indicators.note: redesigned says the letters of the preceding words are rearranged into a new pattern

explanation.surface: Ordinary clothing that's austere when given a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' looks like an adjective about the dress; it is the flag. The letters of DRESS ITS SPARTAN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stars and Stripes is the US national flag, and a standard is a flag or banner.

clue.text: Regularly sail, say, into port

parts.note: a ship that plies a route sails it regularly
to mouth is to say, form words

explanation.surface: Sailing regularly, for example, into a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like an alternate-letter signal, but 'Regularly sail' together means PLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Plymouth is a naval port and city on the Devon coast of England.

clue.text: Surrounded by sailors, one's bearing up

indicators.note: the words that follow surround what came before, so the first pieces go inside

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, sailors
one is I, so one's (one is) gives I and S
a compass bearing such as east gives E

explanation.surface: Among seamen, a person is holding up well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing up' reads as coping, but 'bearing' is the compass point E and 'up' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has risen is up, out of bed or on their feet.

clue.text: Protection provided, yet fasten buckles

indicators.note: buckles here is a verb, bends or distorts, so the letters of the words before are twisted out of shape

explanation.surface: Safety equipment comes with an instruction to do up the straps.
explanation.walkthrough: The text read 'yer'; the page prints 'yet'. 'buckles' is a verb meaning crumples, shuffling the letters of YET FASTEN; 'provided' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety net is a safeguard against hardship, literally the net that catches falling acrobats.

clue.text: Dog Conservative leading vigorous form of government

parts.note: Pluto is Mickey Mouse's dog in the Disney cartoons
racy can mean lively, spirited, vigorous

explanation.surface: A Tory hound heading an energetic style of rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' just places the earlier pieces ahead of RACY.
explanation.definitionFit: Plutocracy is rule by the wealthy, a system of government.

clue.text: Piano providing some parts of tune

indicators.note: providing some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A keyboard instrument supplying fragments of a melody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piano' looks like the instrument, but it is the musical direction meaning quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano is the musical term for quiet, the opposite of loud.

clue.text: About feature, gets strange impressions

indicators.note: about means going round, so the scrambled letters go round the other piece
strange says the letters of the word next to it are made odd, rearranged

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: Concerning a facial trait, someone gets peculiar impressions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as 'concerning', but it is the container signal; 'strange' scrambles the word beside it to ETGS, which wraps round the facial feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Etchings are prints taken from etched plates, impressions made in ink on paper.

clue.text: Fashions are not flowery

indicators.note: fashions is a verb here, shapes or makes, so the letters of the next words are made into a new form

explanation.surface: Trends aren't florid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashions' looks like a noun but is the verb that reshapes ARE NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately decorated, as an overwrought or florid style of writing is.

clue.text: A river, a French or English one

parts.note: un is French for a

explanation.surface: A waterway, either in France or England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Arun is a river in Sussex in southern England, so 'English one' means an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arun is a river in West Sussex, England, flowing to the sea at Littlehampton.

clue.text: Repertory company take exception to play

parts.note: rep is short for a repertory company or theatre
to resent something is to take exception to it

explanation.surface: A theatre troupe objects to staging a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent is to portray or act a part, as an actor plays a role.

clue.text: Mark has not been a revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary says the letters of the words before are turned round into a new order

explanation.surface: Marx was never a revolutionary, someone claims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like a noun about the man named Mark; it is the signal to rearrange NOT BEEN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Nota bene is Latin for note well, an instruction to mark or heed something.

clue.text: I'll go downhill fast if put on ice

definitions.text: I'll go downhill fast if put on ice

parts.words: I'll go downhill fast if put on ice
parts.note: sounds like something deteriorating if shelved, but describes a winter sports vehicle racing down an icy run

explanation.surface: Something says it will quickly deteriorate if postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on ice' suggests being postponed and 'go downhill' suggests decline; read literally, it is a sled on an ice track.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobsleigh is a racing sled that speeds down an iced chute, the literal reading of the clue.

clue.text: Augur warning toxophilite

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning
a toxophilite is an archer, and William Tell is the legendary Swiss archer

explanation.surface: A soothsayer cautions an archer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Augur' looks like a noun for a prophet, but it is the verb meaning to predict.
explanation.definitionFit: To augur is to predict or portend, just as to foretell is to prophesy.

clue.text: False financial undertakings given by 27

parts.note: the answer to 27 across means goad, and another word for goad is spur
IOUs are written promises to pay debts

explanation.surface: Bogus promises of payment issued by a fellow clue.
explanation.walkthrough: '27' points to the clue 27 across, whose answer means a goad: SPUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurious means not genuine, counterfeit, so fake or untrue.

clue.text: Senseless strikes

definitions.meaning: slang for crazy, out of one's mind
... as a verb means hits, as with a bat

explanation.definitionFit: Bats is informal for mad, and to bat something is to hit it.

clue.text: Sharp investigators employed in rising national agency

indicators.note: employed in says one group works inside another, so it goes within
in a down clue, rising means the word is read upward, backwards

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Keen detectives work within an ascendant state body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' only works as a reversal in a down clue, giving AIC; 'employed in' then sets the detectives inside it. CID is the detective branch of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: An acidic taste is sour or tart, which is what sharp means of flavours.

clue.text: Band in the distance

definitions.meaning: a band of allies or a group of sports clubs is a ...
an old measure of distance, about three miles

explanation.surface: A music group playing far off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians; here it is an alliance. 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is an alliance or association, and also an old unit of length of roughly three miles.

clue.text: Train new union member

definitions.meaning: a bridegroom is a new member of a marriage union

explanation.definitionFit: To groom is to coach for a role, and a groom is a man just married.

clue.text: Spots not following second rash

indicators.note: not says what follows is left out of the word before

parts.note: freckles are small brown spots on the skin
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Blemishes appearing after a moment's skin rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like a skin complaint to go with spots, but it is the adjective meaning hasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckless means acting without care for danger, impetuous, just as a rash act is.

clue.text: Notes, rising, onset of rays of sun

parts.note: two notes of the sol-fa scale in ascending order, so then la

indicators.note: onset is the start, so only the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Musical notes ascending as the sun's rays begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' looks like a reversal signal in a down clue, but here it says the notes go up the scale: SO then LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar means relating to or derived from the sun.

clue.text: Not quite the king's champion

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: Herod was the biblical king of Judea

explanation.surface: Not exactly the monarch's defender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the king's' is read as a possessive of the monarch's champion, but it is King HEROD, minus its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero is a champion, someone admired for courage or great deeds.

clue.text: A single shoe — otherwise sell paired

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the letters of the next words are arranged differently

explanation.surface: One shoe alone, or else you might sell them as a pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single' and 'paired' point to footwear sold in pairs; the letters of SELL PAIRED are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An espadrille is a canvas shoe with a rope sole, and the definition names just one of them.

clue.text: Tailless creature in fits about goad

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other
about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to fit someone is to suit them

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter of the word is docked

parts.note: a mule is a creature, a horse and donkey cross

explanation.surface: An animal without a tail flies into rages over a prod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fits' looks like seizures, but it is the verb meaning suits; 'about' turns it to STIUS, 'Tailless' docks the animal's last letter, and 'in' puts the result inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A stimulus is an incentive or spur, something that prods into action as a goad does.

clue.text: Businessman about to be consistent

parts.note: read as two words, business is CO (company) and man is HE
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A trader is about to be dependable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Businessman' splits into business, CO for company, and man, HE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to hang together logically, to form a consistent whole.
